name: Phosphatidylserine
short: Older adults with memory complaints (120 and 157 people): blood tests, blood pressure and heart rate did not differ from placebo; adverse events did not differ in the 120-person trial.
text: In a 12-week trial in 120 older adults with age-associated memory impairment, soy-derived phosphatidylserine at 300 or 600 mg daily produced no significant differences from placebo in standard blood chemistry and blood count tests, blood pressure, heart rate or adverse events. In a 15-week placebo-controlled trial of a marine-sourced phosphatidylserine carrying omega-3 fatty acids in 157 older adults with memory complaints, no safety parameters differed between groups; in the 15-week open-label extension, participants had a reduction in resting diastolic blood pressure and a slight weight gain. In a 2-month trial of soy-derived phosphatidylserine in 36 children aged 4 to 14 with ADHD, it was well tolerated and showed no adverse effects. These trials were small and short. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
